title: The 2-adic Unit Group as an Internal Direct Product: (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ = ⟨−1⟩ × ⟨5⟩
description: The parent (euler-totient-oq-01-oq-02) records, from Mathlib, the value of the Carmichael function λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² for k ≥ 3 — the exponent of (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ. This entry proves the structure theorem that explains that value: for k ≥ 3, (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ is the internal direct product of the order-2 subgroup ⟨−1⟩ and the order-2ᵏ⁻² cyclic subgroup ⟨5⟩, i.e. (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻². The mathematical crux — and the one step genuinely absent from Mathlib — is that −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩, proved by reduction mod 4: every power of 5 is ≡ 1 (mod 4) while −1 ≡ 3 (mod 4). Combined with the order count |⟨−1⟩|·|⟨5⟩| = 2·2ᵏ⁻² = 2ᵏ⁻¹ = |(ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ|, this yields the IsComplement' decomposition. λ(2ᵏ) = lcm(2, 2ᵏ⁻²) = 2ᵏ⁻² then drops out. Verified, 0 axioms.

This obstruction to cyclicity is NOT packaged in Mathlib (which proves only non-cyclicity abstractly and the order of 5).

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: records λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² from Mathlib. This entry proves the underlying group-structure theorem (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ = ⟨−1⟩ × ⟨5⟩ that explains the value.

overview.historicalContext:
For an odd prime power pᵏ the unit group (ℤ/pᵏℤ)ˣ is cyclic, so it has a primitive root and λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ). Powers of two are the exceptional case: (ℤ/2ℤ)ˣ and (ℤ/4ℤ)ˣ are cyclic, but for k ≥ 3 the group (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ has no primitive root. The classical structure theorem (Gauss; see Ireland & Rosen, Ch. 4) says it is instead a direct product of two cyclic groups: ℤ/2, generated by −1, and ℤ/2ᵏ⁻², generated by 5 (equivalently by any element ≡ 3 or 5 mod 8). The exponent of this product is lcm(2, 2ᵏ⁻²) = 2ᵏ⁻², which is exactly λ(2ᵏ) — half of φ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻¹.

Mathlib proves that (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ is not cyclic for k ≥ 3 and that 5 has order 2ᵏ⁻² there, but it does not package the explicit two-generator product decomposition. This entry supplies it. The heart of the matter is that −1 lies outside the cyclic subgroup ⟨5⟩, which is what makes the two factors independent; everything else is an order count.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the structure theorem for the 2-power unit group: for k ≥ 3, (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ is the internal direct product of ⟨−1⟩ (order 2) and ⟨5⟩ (order 2ᵏ⁻²), so (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻² and every unit is uniquely (−1)ᵃ·5ᵇ with a ∈ {0,1}, 0 ≤ b < 2ᵏ⁻². Recover λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² as a consequence.
overview.proofStrategy: Parametrise k = n + 3. (1) Transport ZMod.orderOf_five to the unit group to get orderOf 5 = 2ⁿ⁺¹, and prove orderOf (−1) = 2 by orderOf_eq_prime. (2) The crux: −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩. Build the reduction homomorphism red : (ℤ/2ⁿ⁺³ℤ)ˣ → (ℤ/4ℤ)ˣ from ZMod.castHom (4 ∣ 2ⁿ⁺³). Then red 5 = 1 (since 5 ≡ 1 mod 4) and red (−1) = −1; if 5^m = −1 then applying red gives 1 = −1 in (ℤ/4ℤ)ˣ, refuted by decide. (3) Disjointness ⟨−1⟩ ∩ ⟨5⟩ = ⊥: an element (−1)^m is 1 (m even) or −1 (m odd); the latter would put −1 ∈ ⟨5⟩, contradicting the crux. (4) Count: |⟨−1⟩|·|⟨5⟩| = 2·2ⁿ⁺¹ = 2ⁿ⁺² = φ(2ⁿ⁺³) = |(ℤ/2ⁿ⁺³ℤ)ˣ|. Feed (3) and (4) to isComplement'_of_card_mul_and_disjoint to obtain the IsComplement' decomposition. (5) Recover λ(2ⁿ⁺³) = 2ⁿ⁺¹ via Mathlib's carmichael_two_pow_of_ne_two.
keyInsights: The single fact that makes (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ non-cyclic is that −1 is not a power of 5: powers of 5 stay ≡ 1 (mod 4), but −1 ≡ 3. Reduction mod 4 turns this into a one-line homomorphism argument.
Once −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩ is known, the whole decomposition is an order count: the two cyclic subgroups have orders 2 and 2ᵏ⁻², product 2ᵏ⁻¹ = φ(2ᵏ), and are disjoint, hence complementary.
The structure theorem (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻² explains the parent's value: exponent of a product is the lcm of exponents, and lcm(2, 2ᵏ⁻²) = 2ᵏ⁻² = λ(2ᵏ).
−1 and 5 are explicit generators: every unit mod 2ᵏ is uniquely (−1)ᵃ·5ᵇ, a normal form the abstract non-cyclicity statement does not give.
Parametrising k = n + 3 keeps every exponent (2ᵏ⁻¹, 2ᵏ⁻², 2ᵏ) a genuine power, avoiding all truncated-subtraction friction in the Lean statements.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 166 lines and 11 theorems establishing the classical structure theorem for the 2-power unit group: for k ≥ 3, (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ is the internal direct product ⟨−1⟩ × ⟨5⟩ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻². The mathematical heart is the original lemma −1 ∉ ⟨5⟩, proved by reduction mod 4, which is exactly the obstruction to cyclicity and is not packaged in Mathlib. The parent's λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻² is recovered as the exponent (lcm of the factor orders) of this product.
conclusion.implications: This upgrades the parent's exponent value to the full group-structure statement that explains it, with explicit generators −1 and 5 and a unique normal form (−1)ᵃ·5ᵇ for every unit. It complements the odd-prime-power case (cyclic, primitive roots exist) by exhibiting the precise way 2-power unit groups fail to be cyclic.
openQuestions: Bundle the IsComplement' decomposition into an explicit multiplicative isomorphism (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)ˣ ≃* Multiplicative (ℤ/2) × Multiplicative (ℤ/2ᵏ⁻²), giving the discrete-log normal form (a, b) ↦ (−1)ᵃ·5ᵇ computationally.
